The speed shown on a car’s speedometer is proportional to the rate of rotation of the tyres.
The variation of the diameter of a tyre as it wears introduces an error in the speed shown on the
speedometer.
A car has new tyres of diameter 600 mm. The speedometer is accurately calibrated for this
diameter.
The tyres wear as shown, with 6 mm of material being removed from the outer surface.
not to scale
6 mm
new tyre
worn tyre
What is the error in the speed shown on the speedometer after this wear has taken place?
A
The speed shown is too high by 1%.
B
The speed shown is too high by 2%.
C
The speed shown is too low by 1%.
D
The speed shown is too low by 2%.

hints: Notice the $6 \text{ mm}$ is removed from the outer surface all around the tyre - how much does the full $600 \text{ mm}$ diameter change by?
Recall true car speed is distance per rotation times rotation rate, so $v = \pi D \times f$ for diameter $D$.
Compare the distance the speedometer assumes per rotation using $600 \text{ mm}$ with the true distance using the smaller worn diameter.
walkthrough: The speedometer measures rotation rate $f$ and assumes new-tyre distance per rotation $\pi \times 600 \text{ mm}$.
Wear removes $6 \text{ mm}$ from the radius on each side, so diameter change $= 2 \times 6 \text{ mm} = 12 \text{ mm}$.
Worn diameter $= 600 - 12 = 588 \text{ mm}$, so true distance per rotation is $\pi \times 588 \text{ mm}$.
Shown speed is larger than true speed by about $0.02$, or $2\%$. This is option B

A.explanation: This uses only $6 \text{ mm}$ change in diameter, but wear removes $6 \text{ mm}$ from all round the tyre so diameter falls by $12 \text{ mm}$.

B.explanation: Worn diameter is $12 \text{ mm}$ smaller than $600 \text{ mm}$, so shown speed exceeds true speed by $12/600 = 2\%$.

C.explanation: The direction is wrong: a smaller worn tyre travels less distance per rotation, so the calibrated speedometer over-reads.

D.explanation: Both direction and size are wrong: the reading is too high, not too low, by about $2\%$.
